drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Mutant total protein sits at about 4 to 8 percent of wild type in four of five variants and rises only about 1.05 to 1.65 fold with the class; the soluble fraction roughly doubles (soluble pool about 2 to 4 fold, reader arithmetic); function reaches or exceeds the untreated wild-type range for three of the four low-protein variants (R406H about 44 against about 55 does not; the fifth variant, P335L, has about 65 percent protein and little baseline deficit). The soluble-pool figures combine panels with different loading normalisers and carry a reader error of about plus or minus 10 percent of axis, and fold values near 1.05 are not separable from 1.0. Quantity and function are not proportional (read-out saturation not excluded; the authors report near-wild-type expression in neurons, not overexpression, and a pixel-threshold read-out); a steady-state deficit of about 12 to 25 fold is only about 1.5 to 3 fold explained by the measured turnover.

p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WOREE (Q230P-class missense) as target. Origin contexts: STXBP1, SLC6A1, GABRA1 and GAT-1 variants in cells, worm, fly, zebrafish and mouse (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE). Bridge limit: one precedent of the lot is a soluble cytosolic client (Munc18-1) where the class raised the mutant, but no enzyme and no WWOX system was tested; wild type is raised as well.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test in any WWOX system (registry-based, known-roads note section 2.8, 2026-10-20); no dedicated PubMed query for these molecules was run for this card. 4-PBA/TUDCA were carried as TX-003 and withdrawn on rationale (DIS-004), not on a result. NOT MAI_TENTATO-proof: unpublished individual experience is unreachable by any literature query.
p4_card.state_of_known_roads: inconclusive, narrowed in IT5 P8 (rationale withdrawn once, not refuted; compartment objection not established for a soluble client; no WWOX test; HDAC6 role open).
p4_card.expected_contribution: Function recovery of residual WWOX protein is the only contribution hypothesised; compensation, symptom and protection are not claimed. The branch (retained, cleared, insoluble) must be placed before any contribution can be stated.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: the folding or trafficking fate of a destabilised client; type of action debated among three non-exclusive classes: physical chemical chaperoning (the class and HDAC-free osmolytes both raised a soluble mutant), HDAC6/HSP90-linked acetylation (open for the class: the class engages HDAC6 at applied levels, butyrate does not, one cytosolic enzyme precedent responds to an HDAC6 lever), and class-I HDAC-mediated transcription of the cDNA (a class-I inhibitor did not reproduce the soluble mutant gain, a contrast that assumes butyrate is at least as strong as the class on class-I enzymes, which is document-dependent; promoter and mRNA-under-treatment controls absent). No source curates a chaperone target or potency for the class; its HDAC potencies are quantified at enzyme level and the applied levels sit well above them. Direction: up in protein; context: ER-retained membrane clients and one soluble cytosolic client.

internal: TX-003, DIS-004, D-03 as cited in the known-roads note (arimoclomol-type candidate, withdrawn the same day)

for: Allele-specific rescue of a fully ER-retained variant with protein and function read together (GAT-1 G443V, fly seizure-like episodes down).
Total and surface protein rise in other missense lesions with the class.

In the soluble cytosolic client, the class and two HDAC-free osmolytes raised the mutant while a class-I HDAC inhibitor did not, and the soluble fraction roughly doubled with a vesicle-recycling read-out at or above the untreated wild-type range for three of the four low-protein variants (partial dissociation of quantity from function in the favourable direction; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE).
against: Wild type is raised in every target: the effect is not mutant-specific.
Not rescued: the partly trafficked G443D; null zebrafish (protein not measured); butyrate raised total immature protein with a small, variant-dependent function gain.
Mouse exposures were short (days); no brain exposure measured beside mutant protein; the human arm of one paper is one uncontrolled child.
No enzyme-class precedent for the class; the enzyme precedents use degradation blockade or an active-site binder.

The soluble precedent raises wild type as well, adds no enzyme, no route-inhibitor arm and no mRNA under treatment, uses a dominant-negative mechanism WWOX does not have, and its total-protein gain on four of five mutants is only about 1.05 to 1.65 fold.

A required-fold limit: a boost multiplies the mutant's residual function and does not change it; parity needs the reciprocal of (amount times function per molecule), which is unmeasured for every WWOX allele, and observed gains (about 1.05 to 9 fold) also apply to wild type.

The measured turnover difference (about 1.5 to 3 fold) explains only a small part of a 12 to 25 fold steady-state deficit in the soluble precedent, so the 'made then cleared' branch is not the only candidate even where turnover is measured.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Soluble monomeric client with a dominant-negative mechanism, or ER-retained membrane client, versus a recessive cytosolic SDR enzyme; CMV-promoter plasmid overexpression in cell lines, or lentiviral expression near wild-type level in neurons (authors' statement; saturation or excess not excluded), versus own promoter; wild type raised alike; the in vitro and in vivo gains are protein quantity, not WWOX function.

p4_card.pharmacology: Potency, relevant exposure and selectivity in a WWOX system: UNKNOWN. Re-examined in IT5 (pharmacology_it5_20261029/proteostasis_pba_a01.tsv): the only measured potency for the class is HDAC inhibition, at micromolar to sub-millimolar values (one HeLa extract study: low micromolar; recombinant enzymes: tens to hundreds of micromolar, with butyrate more potent than phenylbutyrate in the same assay and the order reversed in the HeLa study), while the cell experiments in the cited papers applied roughly half a millimolar to ten millimolar for a day (a toxicity ceiling at four millimolar in one paper) and the bile acid one hundred micromolar; so HDAC inhibition is quantitatively available at the concentrations used and cannot be excluded as the operating mechanism, and there is no numeric value for the chaperone mechanism of either compound, although qualitative active records exist for phenylbutyric acid alone (model-protein aggregation suppression and ER-stress cell protection, each at a single concentration and neither on a disease client); the bile acid has no folding or aggregation record In the sources: class not selective for the mutant; brain exposure not measured in any R1 paper. Keyless sources, IT5 P8 re-pull: no folding, binding or thermal-shift datum for the class or TUDCA in ChEMBL, GtoPdb or DGIdb (ChEMBL mechanism of record: ammonia scavenging for the sodium salt, Unknown for TUDCA; GtoPdb no curated interaction for either); the levels applied in cells were about 8 to 78 times the class's HDAC enzyme IC50 (arithmetic, not occupancy); butyrate is 4 to 29 times more potent than the acid on class I in one document (its low values recur in another that lists no phenylbutyrate) but weaker on HDAC1 than the sodium salt in a third, so the relative class-I strength is document-dependent; butyrate does not engage HDAC6 in the one document that tests it.

p4_card.next_measurement: Build the wild-type function ruler first, then fate, then levers. (1) In an isogenic WWOX-null human neural system with one inducible promoter at one landing site, titrate wild-type WWOX across at least five levels and read a WWOX-dependent cell phenotype against measured per-cell protein (Tier 1: glucose uptake or lactate/oxygen consumption, which depends on WW1; Tier 2, binary confirmation only: neuronal Ca2+ firing; design in wwox_function_reference_it6_20261029.md) with antibody blot plus targeted mass spectrometry, soluble, pellet and total fractions, and transgene mRNA in the same wells, with empty/EGFP-null, WW1-dead (W44F/P47A) and isogenic uninduced wild-type arms, and L404A as an SDR-region binding probe only; (2) place the Q230P-class allele on that curve and read a per-molecule binding-competence ratio (WW1-dependent and SDR-region partners) beside it; (3) only then run the three-class lever panel of the IT5 P8 design (class-I HDAC inhibitor without HDAC6 activity; pan-HDAC or HDAC6-selective inhibitor; HDAC-free bile acid and osmolytes with an osmotic control), each also on the null line and on the wild-type ruler line, with the arm-outcome predictions registered in both directions. A result on the Tier 1 curve is read as recovery of the WW1-dependent axis only, not as rescue of SDR-domain function, unless an SDR-region readout also agrees. No abundance gain is read as rescue unless the variant plus compound arm moves along its own ruler curve with mRNA flat and the null line unaffected; a gain at equal protein above the variant's own curve is scored separately as a rise in per-molecule function. No WWOX catalytic activity is assumed or assayed: none is validated.
p4_card.status_reason: Mechanism of the class contested among three classes; rescue allele-specific; rationale withdrawn once and the compartment objection narrowed, not removed; revival trigger partly answered (class-I HDAC action does not reproduce the soluble mutant gain; HDAC6 role open). Deferred until the lesion's fate and a wild-type function ruler exist.
p4_card.value_added: Separates what the class did in other proteins (retained-branch rescue, non-selectivity, non-rescue) from what is unknown for Q230P; corrects the compartment transfer claim (one precedent is a soluble cytosolic client); splits the abundance gain into three mechanistic classes with one measured contrast each; adds the required-fold limit and the arm set the fate experiment needs.
p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (disease-models/wwox/research/drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven separate queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the only synonym-driven record is one observational natural-history registry. Carried with the census's own caution: "A missing hit does not prove that no study exists." It answers seven queries against one registry on one date; unregistered, differently worded, non-NLM or later-registered studies are not excluded.

not_known: Where the Q230P protein is lost: never made, made and cleared, made and insoluble, made and epitope-invisible, or truncated. No fractionation, inhibitor, synthesis or half-life datum exists for the exact variant.

Whether any recovered Q230P protein would carry WWOX function: there is no per-molecule WWOX function assay in the repository, and protein quantity does not imply function (in the R1 lot quantity and function diverged in some systems and function could not be measured in others).

The share of destabilised-missense lesions that are stability lesions for a WWOX SDR-domain variant: the estimates carried in the literature are cited estimates, and the SDR-domain thermal stability is a missing measurement.
No drug has been given to any WWOX model carrying a missense or a splice allele (known-roads note, section 5).
Whether a cytosolic enzyme lesion behaves like the ER-retained branch at all.
Whether the class, if it acts, acts through chaperoning or through raising expression of the allele.
Whether the class acts on a soluble cytosolic mutant through HDAC6/HSP90 acetylation: butyrate does not engage HDAC6 and no pan-HDAC or HDAC6-selective arm exists in the soluble precedent.

The residual function of the Q230P-class protein per molecule and its amount relative to wild type: the reciprocal of their product is the fold gain any boost would need, and neither factor is measured for any WWOX allele.
Whether any function read-out of WWOX saturates below wild-type protein, as the soluble precedent's read-out appears to.
evidence_against: Partly trafficked variant not rescued by the class (glycerol rescued it in vitro).
Rationale withdrawn once in this repository.
Class-I HDAC action does not reproduce the soluble mutant gain, but that does not exclude HDAC6 or transcription-linked effects.
Observed gains also apply to wild type and are small against a deficit of tens of fold.
